long_biography.plain_text:
Stanley Seeger's support for Greek scholarship began with a gift establishing a Hellenic fund at Princeton in 1979. He continued funding the programme for three decades, supporting research collections and enabling students and faculty to travel to Greece. The university named its Hellenic studies centre after him shortly before his death.

His private library reflected a similarly sustained interest in Joseph Conrad. It brought together first editions, presentation copies, letters and the manuscript of Typhoon, which he acquired in 1990. He was still building the collection when he died; it included a volume bearing his father's ownership signature, connecting two generations of readers.
